title: U.S. House · Virginia's 10th District
area: Northern Virginia, including Loudoun County and parts of Prince William and Fairfax counties.

context.text: Incumbent Suhas Subramanyam advanced from the Democratic primary unopposed after it was canceled. Dave Beckwith won the Republican primary with 72.5% of the vote over Julie Perry (20.4%), Anthony Suttles (5.5%) and Sam Wong (1.6%). Cook Political Report, Decision Desk, Inside Elections and Sabato's Crystal Ball all rate the race Solid/Safe Democratic as of September 22, 2026. Two additional independents, Steven Goforth and Omar Morsy, declared as write-in candidates; they are not on the printed ballot and have no entry here.

candidates.name: Suhas Subramanyam
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the Democratic primary unopposed after the primary was canceled.

summary.text: Suhas Subramanyam is the Democratic incumbent seeking a second term representing Virginia's 10th District. A lawyer and former White House technology policy advisor, he previously served in the Virginia House of Delegates and State Senate, where he passed legislation lowering tolls, utility bills and prescription-drug costs.

background.text: Served as a White House technology policy advisor under President Obama; worked in the private sector with tech startups and started his own business.
Served in the Virginia House of Delegates (2019-2023) and the Virginia State Senate (2023-2024), where he co-founded a bipartisan caucus and passed bills on K-12 education, taxes and gun safety.
Earned a B.A. from Tulane University and a J.D. from Northwestern University's Pritzker School of Law; volunteers as a firefighter and EMT with the Loudoun Medical Reserve Corps.

priorities.text: Lowering the cost of tolls, utility bills and prescription drugs, building on legislation he passed in the Virginia legislature.

positions.summary: In a February 2026 statement on U.S. military action in Iran he said the authority to declare war rests with Congress and that the President must seek congressional authorization.
positions.quote: The authority to declare war resides with Congress. As these developments unfold, President Trump must seek proper Congressional authorization.

positions.summary: In a January 2026 statement he called extending the ACA tax credits an imperative and said Congress needs comprehensive changes to make health care more affordable and accessible.
positions.quote: Extending the ACA tax credits has always been an imperative.

record.text: As a Virginia state legislator, passed legislation lowering the costs of tolls, utility bills and prescription drugs.
Co-founded a bipartisan caucus in the Virginia legislature and passed bipartisan bills on K-12 education, tax policy and gun safety.

candidates.name: Dave Beckwith
candidates.ballotNote: Won the August 4, 2026 Republican primary with 72.5% of the vote over Julie Perry, Anthony Suttles and Sam Wong.

summary.text: Dave Beckwith is the Republican nominee challenging incumbent Suhas Subramanyam. A retired Air Force officer who later served as Deputy Assistant Secretary of Defense at the Pentagon, he is running on tax relief, deficit reduction, an "all-of-the-above" energy strategy and support for law enforcement.

background.text: Served 30 years in the U.S. Air Force and later as Deputy Assistant Secretary of Defense at the Pentagon, managing a $500 billion portfolio spanning space systems, nuclear and missile defense, and national intelligence.
background.quote: After 30 years in the Air Force, recent service as Deputy Assistant Secretary of Defense at the Pentagon, and 17 years as your neighbor in Loudoun County, Dave Beckwith believes serving VA-10 is the next right step.

background.text: Earned a B.S. in Aerospace Engineering from the University of Notre Dame and a Master's in Mechanical Engineering from the University of Dayton; is a graduate of the U.S. Army War College.

priorities.text: Keeping the $40,000 SALT deduction permanent, indexing capital gains to inflation and simplifying the tax code.
An "all-of-the-above" energy strategy, including reinvestment in nuclear power.
Disciplined federal spending caps and opposing locking pandemic-era emergency spending into the permanent budget baseline.

statements.quote: Dave believes every family should have the right to direct their child's education, whether that is a public school, a charter school, a private school, a vocational program, or a homeschool curriculum.
These professionals have one of the toughest jobs in the country, and they deserve the resources and backing necessary to do it effectively.
statements.context: On his campaign website, about the U.S. Capitol Police and the Loudoun County Sheriff's Office

statements.quote: This includes a "zero tolerance" approach to criminal illegal aliens; those who break our laws must be tried, punished, and deported.

He supports crisis pregnancy centers across VA-10 that offer free medical care, counseling, and resources to women facing an unplanned pregnancy, so that choosing life also comes with real support behind it.
Dave believes in a true all-of-the-above energy strategy, one that lets the market, not the government, determine the best mix of sources.

candidates.researchNotes: Statements come from Beckwith's campaign website issue pages. He had not answered the WAMU/VPM questionnaire as of Oct. 5, 2026, and no Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey was found. His site states no position on guns beyond the Second Amendment, and none on rent regulation, minimum wage, tariffs, Israel aid or war powers.

candidates.name: Ahsen Malik

summary.text: Ahsen Malik is an independent candidate for Virginia's 10th District, running as a self-described uniter opposed to the two-party system.

background.text: A lifelong Virginia resident who decided to run for Congress after finding only one candidate on the ballot in a past election.

priorities.text: Presenting an independent alternative to the two major parties, arguing voters are underestimating independents' chances of winning.
priorities.quote: The vast majority of Americans are fed up with the corruption and failure of the two-party duopoly and want real change.

priorities.text: Says he will fight for a balanced budget as the key to reducing inflation over the long term.
priorities.quote: I will fight hard for a balanced budget as that is the key to reducing inflation long term and preventing it from coming back

priorities.text: Wants Congress to put public service ahead of personal interest and to end government shutdowns.
priorities.quote: Too many politicians in Washington put their careers and party first, and the people they serve second.

priorities.text: Supports replacing the Electoral College with ranked-choice voting through a constitutional amendment.
priorities.quote: replacing the Electoral College with ranked-choice voting

positions.summary: Describes support for guaranteeing abortion access early in pregnancy and a federal ban later, with an exception when the pregnancy threatens the mother's life; names two compromise proposals (15 weeks or 9/19 weeks).
positions.quote: I am pro-choice in the first trimester and pro-life in the last trimester with the exception of the pregnancy being harmful to the life of the mother

positions.summary: Supports a single-payer health insurance system covering all Americans, through either a state-based Medicaid-for-all or a federal Medicare-for-all model.
positions.quote: I support a Single Payer Health Insurance System covering all Americans

positions.summary: Supports immigration enforcement and a secure border, opposes mass deportation of undocumented immigrants already in the country, and proposes permanent legal residency without a path to citizenship.
positions.quote: I support immigration enforcement and a secure border

positions.summary: Supports a bipartisan climate bill that expands clean and renewable energy with capped, time-limited incentives, and says moving too fast away from fossil fuels before alternatives exist at scale risks price spikes.
positions.quote: I support a bipartisan climate bill that aggressively expands clean and renewable energy

positions.summary: Says Congress, not the President, holds the power to declare war and that he would work to restore that authority.
positions.quote: I will work to restore that authority, so that no future president can lead us into another unnecessary war.

candidates.researchNotes: Positions come from Malik's campaign website issue pages and his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey (submitted Oct. 6, 2026). He had not answered the WAMU/VPM questionnaire as of Oct. 5, 2026. No stance was found on guns, tariffs, Israel aid or transgender athletes.
